title: House mark is no free pass

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. Your client sells under its own house mark, but uses a rival's registered word to describe the product. Is that a defence?
On the twenty seventh of October, twenty twenty six, a single bench of Honourable Justice C S Dias of the Kerala High Court ruled.
scenes.shown: On 27 October 2026, a single bench of Honourable Justice C.S. Dias of the Kerala High Court ruled.

scenes.dialogue: Wipro says it acquired the Brahmins group business, with its trademark, in twenty twenty three. It sued Greenmount Spices, whose sambar powder carries that word in its name.
scenes.shown: Wipro says it acquired the Brahmins group business, with its trademark, in 2023. It sued Greenmount Spices, whose sambar powder carries that word in its name.

scenes.dialogue: In April, an Ernakulam court granted a temporary injunction. Greenmount appealed, arguing that the trial court treated a mere description as its trademark.
Its case: the trademark is Greenmount, and the other words only describe the product, a use protected by Section Thirty, sub section Two, clause A, of the Trade Marks Act.
scenes.shown: Its case: the trademark is Greenmount, and the other words only describe the product, a use protected by Section 30(2)(a) of the Trade Marks Act.

scenes.dialogue: The Court held: calling a registered word descriptive is no unrestricted licence. What matters is whether, in context, it genuinely describes the goods.
Equally, registration alone doesn't prove infringement. And Greenmount's house mark, or peaceful co existence, is no answer by itself. These are matters for trial.
scenes.shown: Equally, registration alone doesn't prove infringement. And Greenmount's house mark, or peaceful co-existence, is no answer by itself. These are matters for trial.

scenes.dialogue: Prima facie, documents date the brand to nineteen eighty seven; on Greenmount's own case, its use began in twenty eleven. That backs Wipro's claim of prior use.
scenes.shown: Prima facie, documents date the brand to 1987; on Greenmount's own case, its use began in 2011. That backs Wipro's claim of prior use.

scenes.dialogue: Seeing no perversity, the Court dismissed the appeal, so the interim injunction stays. The findings are tentative; the suit will be decided at trial, free of them.
